pnl_definition: Gross trading P&L = dollar investment gains across all D. E. Shaw group funds and managed accounts (alternatives such as Composite, Oculus, Valence and Cogence, plus long-oriented/active equity, multi-asset and private vehicles) BEFORE management and performance fees, calendar year, USD millions (approximately average investment capital x gross return). D. E. Shaw Research is excluded. The firm publishes no P&L, revenue or financial statements, so every row is derived or estimated: for 2022-2025 the LCH Investments (Edmond de Rothschild) single-year net gains to investors (which are AFTER fees and appear to cover hedge funds/alternatives only) are grossed up for fees and a modelled long-oriented book is added; for 2020-2021 average alternatives capital x reported net Composite/Oculus returns is grossed up the same way; 2015-2019 and 2026 YTD are model estimates without any firm-specific return data. This is not the firm's own revenue (its fee income is only a fraction of these gains).
headcount_definition: Total employees of the D. E. Shaw group worldwide, approximately at year end (2026: latest known figure), taken from the firm's own website ('more than X people': >1,000 late 2014, >1,200 2018, >1,300 Dec 2019, >1,700 Nov 2020, >1,900 Dec 2021, >2,000 Dec 2022-Sep 2023, >2,500 Mar 2024-Dec 2025, >3,000 Feb-Oct 2026). These are lower bounds without precise as-of dates, so mids sit somewhat above the floor and gaps (2015-2017, 2023-2025) are interpolated. Form ADV Item 5A employee counts (435 in FY2015 rising to 998 in FY2025) are NOT used: they cover only the US registered adviser and its relying advisers and exclude D. E. Shaw India and other non-adviser affiliates, so they are roughly one-third of the group. It is not stated whether the website figure includes contractors or D. E. Shaw Research; bands allow for this.
fx_note: All inputs are in USD (LCH, press, deshaw.com and SEC figures); no currency conversion was needed.
methodology: Synthesized from two completed research lenses (press and primary filings/company website); no new searches were run. Investment capital comes from archived deshaw.com snapshots (lower-bound 'more than' figures), averaged within each year; regulatory AUM from Form ADV is leverage-inflated and only noted. For 2022-2025, LCH single-year net gains ($8.2bn, $4.2bn, $11.1bn, $12.7bn; chain-checked against the cumulative $56.1bn, $67.2bn and $79.9bn) are grossed up using fee-paying share ~65-75%, performance fee ~30-33% and management fee ~3%, and estimated gains on the ~$18-25bn long-oriented book are added; 2020-2021 use average alternatives capital x reported Composite/Oculus net returns with the same gross-up. 2015-2019 and 2026 YTD have no firm-specific returns in the evidence, so they are capital x assumed long-run returns (Composite/Oculus annualised net ~12.5-14%) plus equity-market-like returns on the long book, cross-checked against the primary lens's Monte Carlo, with wide bars. Headcount uses the group-wide website figure; Form ADV counts are cited only to show the subset trap.

Alternatives ~$55-60bn at an assumed ~20%/yr gross (long-run ~13% net grossed up) for 9 months = ~$8.7bn, plus ~$30-35bn long-only/privates (Rupak Ghose estimate ~$35bn) at an assumed ~10%/yr = ~$2.4bn. ytd_2026.description: ESTIMATED, NOT REPORTED. The evidence contains no 2026 Composite, Oculus or LCH figure. The latest capital datapoint is >$115bn 'investment and committed capital' as of 2026-09-01 and the latest headcount is >3,000 (deshaw.com, accessed 2026-10-08). PnL is ~9 months of assumed long-run gross returns on ~$90bn average earning capital: mid $12.0bn, 90% band $3.0-25.0bn.

caveats: Headcount trap: Form ADV Item 5A employee counts (FY2023 879, FY2024 928, FY2025 998) cover only the US registered adviser plus relying advisers and exclude D. E. Shaw India and other affiliates. Aggregators such as FINTRX repeat 998 as firm headcount. The group-wide website figure (~2,500 for 2024-2025, >3,000 in 2026) is used instead. Website figures are lower bounds that move in steps, and the Jun-to-Nov 2020 jump (>1,400 to >1,700) may be partly definitional.

Regulatory AUM ($77-128bn in 2015-2023, $154.6bn FY2024, $213.4bn FY2025) and Schedule D gross asset values (Composite $91bn, Oculus $56bn) are leverage-inflated, about 2.5-3x investment capital. They are never used as the capital base.

LCH figures are net of fees, are LCH estimates, and appear to cover only hedge funds/alternatives (2023's $4.2bn matches ~9% on ~$45bn of alternatives). They are grossed up, and long-oriented gains are added by model, so every PnL row is derived or estimated, never reported.
Single-year vs cumulative: $56.1bn (2023), $67.2bn (2024) and $79.9bn (2025) are LCH since-inception totals. TipRanks wrongly reports $56.1bn as 2023 profit; the single-year 2023 figure is $4.2bn.

Annual fund returns come from 'people familiar' (Bloomberg/Reuters), not firm disclosures. Many syndications recycle one report, and sources differ slightly (Composite 2021 18.5% vs 18.8%; 2022 24.6% vs 24.7%; Oculus 2022 20% vs 20.1%). Oculus 2020-2021 rests on a blog citing Bloomberg.

2015-2019 have no D. E. Shaw-specific return or gain data in the evidence. These rows are model estimates using assumed long-run fund returns and broad equity-market-like returns for the long book (an assumption from outside the evidence), so bars are wide.

The capital definition widened in 2018 to 'investment and committed capital', and the 2025-2026 jump (>$70bn to >$115bn) coincided with a redesigned page, retained 2025 profits and new launches. Since 2018 profits have been returned annually (virtually all of 2023, half of 2024, none of 2025), so capital-based estimates are sensitive to timing.

The gross-up assumptions (fee-paying share, Composite performance fee raised from 30% to 35% c.2022, Oculus from 25% to 30%, ~3% management fee) carry ~+/-15% uncertainty on the alternatives gross figure. The size and returns of the long-oriented/active-equity book (~$18-35bn) are not disclosed annually.
D. E. Shaw founder Rich List income ($900m 2022, $750m 2023, $1.6bn 2024, $2.0bn 2025; he owns ~70%) is a consistency cross-check only, not PnL.
open_questions: Composite and Oculus net returns for 2015-2019 and LCH single-year net gains for 2015-2021, e.g. from early-January Bloomberg/Reuters articles and LCH tables (chain back from cumulative $51.9bn at end-2022).
Any 2026 YTD fund return (monthly/quarterly Bloomberg reports), and whether the Jun-Sep 2026 capital jump to >$115bn reflects gains, private commitments or scope.

Size and annual returns of the long-oriented/active-equity, multi-asset and private books (2018 split was $28bn alternatives / $22bn long-oriented; Rupak Ghose puts long-only plus privates ~$35bn in 2026).
Whether the website headcount includes D. E. Shaw Research, contractors or interns, and how large D. E. Shaw India is.
Share of internal/employee (fee-free) capital in the alternatives funds, which drives the gross-up.
LCH's end-2025 AUM of $72.4bn vs the firm's >$85bn, and an unverified LCH end-2024 AUM claim of $41.1bn.
